1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust upward bias by 3–5% for the first 5–7 days.

2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–4% in the 3–5 day window following a spike.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day average of history is below 68, forecast should be capped at 68–70; if above 72, cap at 72–74.

4. Forecast lags true price by 1–3 days in the first 10 days — shift forecast 1–2 days forward for early horizon (days 1–10).

5. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day forecast — increase forecast by 1–3% for last 5 days to align with observed downward trend.

6. If history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive days falling >1%), reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in continuation.

7. Avoid forecasting above 75 unless confirmed by 3+ consecutive days of price above 74 — cap forecasts at 75 if no strong bullish signal in history.
